name: 2011 livery (flying lady)
description: All-white with a big red 'Virgin' signature climbing the white fin, 'virgin australia' in light dark-gray lowercase over the forward windows, the flying-lady nose art holding an Australian flag, a red ring round each engine and red winglets.

sources.title: Virgin Australia (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Virgin Blue rebranded as Virgin Australia in 2011, with this white livery and the flying-lady nose art.

logos.description: The Virgin signature: 'Virgin' in red brush script, very large, rising diagonally (about 55 degrees) up the white fin from its root to the tip; the V's long stroke crosses under the word and its foot dips onto the rear fuselage below the fin. A wordmark: draw it as lettering, no shape proposed.

The flying lady: a reclining woman in dark-gray line drawing, one arm stretched forward, holding a waving Australian flag (in color on the MAX), on the nose below and aft of the cockpit windows; each aircraft's name (a beach or place, e.g. 'Brighton Beach') in small gray type beneath.

titles.style: Light geometric sans, all lowercase, single-storey a and g, tall ascenders, over the windows from the first door to over the wing.

notes: No visible change between 2018 (737-800) and 2025 (737 MAX 8) photos: the 2022-23 brand refresh did not repaint the aircraft as far as photos show, and the older 737-800s and the MAX wear the same scheme. The flag in the flying lady looks colored on the MAX and monochrome on older aircraft (not certain). 'height' of the title is the ascender height; the lowercase x-height is about 0.36. Each aircraft carries its own name under the nose art (not drawn). Re-checked 2026-11-15 on VH-8IE (737 MAX 8, the 737-800's fuselage), placed by its doors and overwing exits: the title runs 0.147 to 0.462, its baseline just over the window tops; the lowercase stands 0.67 of the ascenders (type.xHeight, measured as on the photo).
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximation (which had a red-and-purple fin, closer to the Virgin Blue era). Introduced in 2011 when Virgin Blue became Virgin Australia.
